problem.h2: Most website visitors leave without ever asking a question.
problem.body: Live chat only works when someone's watching it. Contact forms get ignored. FAQ pages get skipped. Meanwhile visitors leave with unanswered questions and no way to reach you outside office hours. WelcoChat stays on your site around the clock, answers from your own content, and only pulls in a human when the conversation actually needs one.

painItems: Visitors leave without getting an answer
Support/sales teams can't staff live chat 24/7
Contact-form leads arrive with no context
FAQ pages exist but visitors don't read them
Good leads go cold waiting for a reply

items.q: How fast can I get WelcoChat live on my site?
items.a: Minutes — create an account, connect your content, paste one embed snippet.

items.q: Does the agent ever make things up?
items.a: No. It only answers from the content you've connected. If it's not confident, it hands off to a human instead of guessing.

items.q: What happens when the agent can't answer?
items.a: Your team is notified immediately by email (or Slack/Teams/webhook on Business+) and can join that conversation and reply live from the portal.

items.q: Do I need a credit card to start?
items.a: No — every account gets a 14-day free trial with no card required.

items.q: Can I use WelcoChat on more than one website?
items.a: Each subscription covers one website. For additional websites, create an additional subscription — contact us if you're setting up several.

items.q: Can visitors reach the agent on WhatsApp too?
items.a: Yes, on the Business plan and above — connect your own WhatsApp Business number and the same agent answers there too, with the same live handoff.

items.q: Can more than one person on my team manage the agent?
items.a: Yes, on the Business plan and above — invite teammates to your WelcoChat account.

items.q: Can I use my own logo and pick which side the widget opens on?
items.a: Yes, on the Business plan and above. Enterprise also adds a custom CSS override for further fine-tuning.
The agent detects and responds in the visitor's language automatically.

items.q: Can I see what visitors are asking?
items.a: Yes — the statistics dashboard shows conversation volume, handoff rate and leads, and every handed-off conversation is visible in Live Chat.

items.q: What happens if my trial ends or my subscription lapses?
items.a: The widget pauses on your website until billing is resolved — visitors just won't see it, not a broken chat. Your portal access and everything you've configured stay untouched, and it all picks back up the moment your subscription is active again.
Yes — upgrade or downgrade anytime from the portal. Nothing you've configured is ever deleted on a downgrade; features tied to a higher tier just pause until you upgrade again.
Yes, on the Business plan and above — visitors can attach a photo and the agent actually looks at it before replying, not just the accompanying text.

items.q: Can I update my website's content after I've gone live?
items.a: Yes — change the connected website URL or edit your uploaded documents and notes anytime from the portal; WelcoChat re-learns the new content with no downtime.

items.q: Does the widget slow down my site or work on mobile?
items.a: It loads asynchronously so it never blocks your page, and it's fully usable on phones and tablets.

guidePromptContent.h1: How to prepare content for your agent
guidePromptContent.sub: A practical guide to getting good answers out of WelcoChat
guidePromptContent.intro: WelcoChat only answers from content you've explicitly connected — your website and anything you upload. It never invents facts, and if it doesn't have an answer in its content, it hands off to your team instead of guessing. That means the quality of your agent depends almost entirely on the quality of what you give it. This guide covers both sources: the automatic website crawl and the "Additional docs / FAQs" notes field.

sections.h2: 1. What the website crawl picks up well
sections.body: When you connect a website URL, WelcoChat crawls the public pages and extracts their text. It works best on pages written in plain language for humans:
list: An FAQ page, if you have one — this is usually the single highest-value page to have crawled
Shipping, returns, warranty and other policy pages
sections.after: It does not extract information trapped in images, PDFs linked but not embedded as text, or JavaScript-rendered content that never appears in the page's HTML. If key information lives in a brochure PDF or a scanned image, upload it as a document instead (see below) rather than assuming the crawl caught it.

sections.h2: 2. What to put in "Additional docs / FAQs"
sections.body: This free-text field is where you fill gaps the website doesn't cover, and where you can shape how the agent talks about your business. It's read the same way as crawled content — as source material to answer from — so treat it as a written brief, not a casual note. Good things to include:
list: Answers to questions you get asked often that aren't clearly written anywhere on your site
Internal shorthand or product names spelled out ("when someone says 'the Pro plan' they mean...")
Tone guidance: "Keep answers short and friendly", "Never discuss competitors", "Always mention the free trial when relevant"
Anything that changes seasonally and won't be on the site yet (an upcoming sale, a temporary shipping delay)
sections.after: Keep it organized under short headings or as a Q&A list — the agent handles structured, scannable text better than one long paragraph.

sections.body: PDF, DOCX and TXT files are supported, up to 10 MB each. The system extracts the text layer — a document has to actually contain selectable text, not just a scanned image of a page, for this to work. If you're not sure, try selecting text in the PDF with your cursor; if you can't, the agent won't be able to read it either.
sections.after: Good candidates: product spec sheets, a detailed FAQ document, policy documents, price lists, onboarding guides.

list_strong.text: If your site says one price and an uploaded doc says another, the agent has no way to know which is current — it may pick either. Keep one source of truth per fact.
A 200-page internal wiki export with meeting notes and half-finished drafts mixed in makes it harder for the agent to find the actually-relevant answer. Curate before you upload.

list_strong.strong: Anything you wouldn't want a visitor to potentially see verbatim.
list_strong.text: The agent answers by drawing directly on connected content — don't include internal pricing negotiated for specific clients, unreleased plans, or anything confidential.

sections.h2: 5. A note on how answers are generated
sections.body: The widget only displays plain conversational text — no Markdown formatting, no tables, no bullet lists render as such. Your source content can be formatted however you like (headings, bullet points, tables are all fine to write), but write your own "Additional docs" notes as plain sentences where possible, since that's closest to what the agent will actually produce back to a visitor.

You can re-crawl your website or edit your notes and documents anytime from the setup page — changes to notes and documents take effect immediately, and re-crawling a changed website takes about a minute. There's no downtime while it updates.

guideSlackTeams.sub: Get a message the moment a visitor needs a human
guideSlackTeams.intro: WelcoChat notifies your team by posting to a webhook URL you provide — there's no app to install or OAuth permission to grant on your side. You create the webhook in Slack or Teams, paste the URL into your WelcoChat setup page's Notifications section, and you're done. This works the same way for the generic webhook option (Zapier, Make, or any tool that can receive an incoming webhook).

steps: Go to api.slack.com/apps and sign in to your workspace.
Click Create New App → From scratch. Give it a name (e.g. "WelcoChat") and pick your workspace.
In the app's settings, open Incoming Webhooks in the left sidebar.
Toggle Activate Incoming Webhooks to on.
Scroll down and click Add New Webhook to Workspace.
Choose the channel that should receive handoff notifications, and click Allow.
Copy the Webhook URL that appears (starts with https://hooks.slack.com/services/...).
In WelcoChat, go to your service's setup page → Notifications, set Channel to Slack, and paste the URL.

teams.intro: Microsoft has been migrating Teams channels from the old "Connectors" (Office 365 Connector) system to Workflows — use Workflows if it's available in your tenant.
steps: Open the Teams channel that should receive handoff notifications.
Click the ⋯ (more options) next to the channel name → Workflows.
Search for and select the template "Post to a channel when a webhook request is received".
Follow the prompts to confirm the channel, then click Create flow (or Add workflow).
Copy the webhook URL Teams generates for you.
In WelcoChat, go to your service's setup page → Notifications, set Channel to Microsoft Teams, and paste the URL.
teams.note: If your tenant still only has the legacy "Incoming Webhook" connector available instead of Workflows, that also works the same way — add the Incoming Webhook connector to the channel, copy its URL, and paste it in the same place.

generic.body: Choose Webhook as the channel and paste the "catch hook" URL from your automation tool. WelcoChat sends a JSON payload with the event type, a message, and relevant IDs (instance and conversation) — build your automation around whatever fields you need from that payload.

testing.body: After saving a channel and webhook URL, use the Send test message button on the setup page — it sends one real notification through the same path a live handoff would use, so you can confirm it lands in the right place before you rely on it.

guideInstall.h1: Add the widget to your website
guideInstall.sub: Works with WordPress, Wix, GoDaddy, Squarespace, Shopify, and any site that lets you paste custom code
guideInstall.intro: The WelcoChat widget is a single line of code — a <script> tag with your agent's own ID. Once your agent is live, copy the snippet from your service's setup page in the portal, then paste it into your site using the instructions below for the platform you use. The widget then appears automatically on every page — no design work, and nothing to install per page.

steps: From your WordPress dashboard, go to Plugins → Add New, search for "WPCode" (or "Insert Headers and Footers"), and install and activate it.
Open the plugin — usually under Code Snippets → Header & Footer in the sidebar.
Paste your WelcoChat snippet into the Footer box, so it loads after your page content.
Click Save. The widget now appears on every page of your site.
Tip: if your theme already has a "Custom Code" or "Header/Footer Scripts" setting — many Elementor and Astra themes do — you can paste the snippet there directly instead of installing a plugin.
Open your site in the Wix Editor and go to Settings → Custom Code (or search "Custom Code" in the top search bar).
Click + Add Custom Code.
Paste your WelcoChat snippet into the code box.
Under Add Code to Pages, choose All Pages. Under Place Code in, choose Body – end.
Click Apply, then publish your site.

In your GoDaddy Website Builder (Websites + Marketing) dashboard, go to Settings → Site-wide Code (on some plans this is under Settings → Advanced Tools → Custom Code; available from the Commerce plan up).
Paste your WelcoChat snippet into the Footer or Body code box.
Click Save and republish your site.
If your GoDaddy plan doesn't include a code-injection option, or your site is actually GoDaddy-hosted WordPress, use the WordPress steps above instead.
In the Squarespace dashboard, go to Settings → Advanced → Code Injection (requires a Business plan or higher).
Paste your WelcoChat snippet into the Footer box, so it loads on every page.
Click Save.
From your Shopify admin, go to Online Store → Themes.
On your current theme, click Edit code.
Open theme.liquid under the Layout folder.
Paste your WelcoChat snippet right before the closing </body> tag.
Click Save.

generic.body: Every other platform we've seen — Webflow, Weebly, Jimdo, Carrd, Framer, a hand-coded site, or your own CMS — works the same way: look for a setting called "Custom Code", "Header & Footer Scripts", "Code Injection", or "Tracking Codes" — this is usually the same place widgets like live-chat tools and analytics scripts get added — and paste the snippet there so it loads on every page. If your site is plain hand-written HTML, paste the snippet directly before the closing </body> tag of each page template.

verify.body: After publishing, open your live site in a new browser tab — not the editor preview — and you should see the WelcoChat bubble in the bottom corner. If it doesn't appear within a minute, double-check the snippet was pasted exactly as copied (including both quote marks), and that any page cache your platform or a plugin (e.g. WP Rocket) uses has been cleared.
